titulo.estudio: Rico en fibra, bajo en sal
titulo.alumno: High in fibre, low in salt

intro: How to read a label and talk about what we eat and what state it is in.

palabras.consejo: It is more technical than «comida» and common on labels and on TV.
After «en» comes what it contains: «rico en hierro». It agrees: «ricos en fibra».
The opposite of «rico en»: «bajo en sal», «baja en grasas». It changes with gender.
Careful: English «preservative» is «conservante». «Preservativo» is something very different.
It comes from «color». On labels it goes next to «conservante»: «sin colorantes».
It is said of food and of documents: «un yogur caducado», «un carné caducado».
It comes from «pudrirse». It is said of fruit, vegetables or meat: «una manzana podrida».
Almost always plural. They are not vegetables: «lentejas», «garbanzos» and «judías».
It is almost always plural: «un puñado de frutos secos».
It does not include fish: menus say «pescados y mariscos».
It works for masculine and feminine: «pan integral», «harina integral». Only the plural changes.
The h is silent: «a-RI-na». It is made from wheat, corn and other cereals.
It comes from «nutrir», to feed. A nutritious meal gives the body what it needs.
The e changes: «digiero», «digieres», «digiere». A heavy meal is hard to digest.
Stress the last syllable: «se-re-AL». The plural «cereales» is the same word used for many grains.
«fibra» is stressed on the first syllable, so it is FI-bra. It is a feminine noun, so say «la fibra».
Notice the «v» is pronounced «b»: «con-ser-BAN-tes». Think of the word «conservar», to keep.
It comes from «color». Here the «o» is open and clear: «ko-lo-RAN-tes».
The pronoun «lo» attaches to the infinitive: «poner» + «lo» = «ponerlo».
It is the feminine form of «caducado», so it agrees with a feminine noun such as «la leche».
«podrida» means rotten; the plural form «podridas» agrees with «fresas».
The «-emos» ending here means «let us». Compare «compramos» (we buy).
Say it with the stress on «TI»: «nu-tri-TI-vos». It comes from «nutrir», to nourish.
The plural «cereales» keeps the same sound as the singular, only with an «-es» at the end.
«rico» means rich or tasty. Use «ricos» when the noun is masculine plural.
«tostada» agrees with the feminine noun «harina». It comes from «tostar», to toast.
«saco» is a large bag. Its stress is on the first syllable: SA-kos.
«pala» is feminine: «la pala». Note that «palo» is a stick, a different word.
The «d» between vowels is soft: «al-MEN-dra». The stress is on «MEN».
«sabor» is masculine and has the stress at the end: sa-BOR. Note «saber» is to know, not to taste.
«bote» is masculine: «el bote». The stress is on «BO»: BO-te.
The «z» and «c» before «i» sound like «th» in Spain: «ka-du-thi-DAD».
«abeja» is feminine: «la abeja». The «j» sounds like a strong «h» in Spanish: a-BE-ha.
«flor» is feminine: «la flor». Its stress is on the only syllable: FLOR.
The «ñ» sounds like «ny» in «canyon»: «a-kom-PA-ña».
«poca» agrees with a feminine noun, like «poca sal». Use «poco» with masculine nouns.
«garbanzos» is masculine plural: «los garbanzos». Pronounce the «z» as «th» in Spain.

texto:
**What it contains.** A food can be **rico en** fibre, vitamins or iron, and **bajo en** salt, sugar or fats. With **sin** you say what it does not contain: **sin conservantes**, **sin colorantes**, **sin gluten**.

**What state it is in.** With **estar**: **está caducado** (it is past its date) and **está podrido** (it has gone bad).

**Ser or estar.** **Es bueno** means it is healthy or of good quality. **Está bueno** means it tastes good.

**Food groups.** **Las legumbres** (lentils, chickpeas), **los frutos secos** (almonds, walnuts) and **el marisco** (prawns, mussels). Bread and flour can be **integrales**.

**False friend.** English «preservative» is **conservante** in Spanish; **preservativo** is something else.

piezas.titulo: Rico en, bajo en, sin, and ser or estar
texto:
**Rico en / bajo en + noun.** The adjective agrees with the food: **un yogur bajo en grasa**, **unos cereales ricos en fibra**, **una bebida baja en azúcar**.

**Sin + noun** says what is missing: **sin sal**, **sin conservantes**. It takes no article.

**Ser or estar** changes the meaning of the adjective:

- **Es bueno** / **es malo**: healthy or harmful, of good or bad quality.
- **Está bueno** / **está malo**: it tastes good or it has gone off.

The state of food goes with **estar**: **está caducado**, **está podrido**.

ejemplos.alumno: These cereals are high in fibre.

ejemplos.estudio: El pan sin conservantes está muy bueno.
ejemplos.alumno: The bread without preservatives tastes very good.

ejemplos.estudio: El pescado fresco es bueno para la salud.
ejemplos.alumno: Fresh fish is good for your health.

opciones.explicacion: Yes: «bajo en» says it has little of something.
That is «rico en sal». «Bajo en» is the opposite.
That would be «sin sal». «Bajo en» allows a little.

frase.texto: Las legumbres son ricas en hierro

pregunta.texto: Which sentence says it tastes good?

opciones.explicacion: That says it is healthy or good quality, not how it tastes.
That says it is out of date, not that it tastes good.

pregunta.texto: How is a yoghurt that is past its date?

opciones.explicacion: Yes: «caducado» is what is past its date.
It is said of fruit or meat that smells bad, not of the date.
That is said of bread or flour, not of yoghurt.

pregunta.texto: Which of these foods is a pulse?

opciones.explicacion: Yes: chickpeas, lentils and beans are pulses.
